title: Committed rate protection, credit orchestration, and autoscale interlock for Dedicated
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Purpose: Define a clear, legally defensible commitment for Reserved Dedicated capacity that protects customer committed-rate expectations while minimizing blast radius for Redwood and enabling predictable remediation. Scope: (1) SLA metric definition for committed serve rate (tokens/minute or RPS equivalent) across an agreed serving corridor, (2) formal error-budget accounting and credit calculation tied to measurable telemetry, (3) contractual notice windows and remediation ladder, and (4) autoscaler interlock rules and fleet control policies that interact with credits and customer entitlements.

Key design decisions we need to finalize: measurement window (sliding vs fixed), quantile(s) to use for compliance (p95 vs p99), aggregation level (per-customer, per-tenant-AZ), definition of acceptable degradation (grace band), how autoscale actions (burst autoscale, emergency burst capacity, prioritized queueing) affect measured entitlement, and the precise crediting formula (proportional to tokens lost vs flat-day credits).

Measurement signals: primary source will be Dedicated telemetry pipeline (per-tenant token throughput and success/error classification) with backup using edge ingress logs and request-level observability in Console. All measurements must be auditable and reproducible by both parties. Legal artifacts: include short templated language for contract SLO, sample credit calculation appendix, and a customer-facing remediation playbook.
acceptance_criteria: SLA definition document approved by product, infra, and legal (includes metric name, aggregation window, quantile, and failure threshold)
Error budget accounting spreadsheet and reference implementation (Python script) that computes credits from telemetry for a given window
Contract language draft (customer-facing and internal) with examples and notice windows reviewed by Legal and Sales

Autoscaler interlock spec that documents how autoscale events are treated for SLA measurement (e.g., preemptive autoscale, emergency burst) and an implementation plan for ENG to enforce interlock flags
Console dashboard mock showing committed-rate vs observed-rate with error budget burn visualization and downloadable CSV for audits
Runbook for incident response and credit application, including escalation paths and SLA communication templates
updates: 2025-02-12 - AM: Initial RFC posted. Raised question about p95 vs p99 as primary compliance quantile; recommended p95 for token-rate SLAs to avoid over-crediting for short tail events.

2025-02-14 - LO: Meeting with Infra (ENG-5820) and SRE. Agreed to measure at 1-minute granularity and compute sliding-window 1h quantiles. ENG will prototype the telemetry aggregator. Action: ENG to provide sample dataset by 2025-02-20.

2025-02-17 - Legal review: Redline of contract language emphasizing clear notice and cure periods; requested explicit clause for force majeure and third-party cloud provider outages. Legal asked for deterministic credit formula rather than subjective remediation.

2025-02-19 - Product sync: Decided on a tiered credit formula: (1) immediate proportional credits for short degradations (<6 hours) computed as lost tokens / committed tokens over the window; (2) capped monthly credit for long degradations with staged remediation ladder; (3) ability for customers to request on-demand capacity during outage with subsequent billing reconciliation.

2025-02-21 - Draft dashboards uploaded: Console team provided mockups for committed-rate vs observed-rate with error budget burn and exportable audit CSV. Pending legal sign-off of customer-facing language.
2025-02-21 - Next steps: Product to consolidate contract appendix & sample calculations; ENG to complete telemetry prototype and provide accuracy report; Sales to review draft for commercial impacts.
risks: Measurement divergence: customer-side telemetry vs our aggregated metric may not perfectly align, leading to disputes
Autoscale ambiguity: if autoscaler preempts capacity transparently, customers may view bursts as failures unless contract language clarifies treatment
Financial exposure: aggressive crediting (flat-day credits) could be expensive during multi-hour outages; need capped formulas
Implementation complexity: per-tenant sliding-window quantiles at minute granularity increase storage/compute on telemetry pipeline
decision_log: 2025-02-14: Chosen measurement granularity = 1 minute; sliding 1h quantile window for compliance calculation (decision by Product + Infra)
2025-02-19: Adopted tiered credit formula (proportional short-window credits, capped monthly remediation credits) (decision by Product + Finance + Legal)

2025-02-20: Autoscale interlock rule: Autoscale-triggered capacity additions will be excluded from historical credit calculations for the immediate 15 minutes after action; beyond that window they are treated as normal capacity (decision by Infra + SRE)
customer_examples: Example A - 99,000 committed tokens per hour (1,650 tokens/min). Observed 1,200 tokens/min averaged over a 2h window -> lost tokens = (1,650-1,200)*120 = 54,000. Credit = 54,000 / (1,650*120) = 27% of those 2 hours' billable tokens (applied as prorated credit).

Example B - Short tail event (30 minutes) where p95 dipped below commitment but p99 within tolerance: No credit if total lost tokens < 0.5% of committed tokens in the billing window as per grace band clause.

Example C - Multi-day degradation: After 24 hours continuous degradation, apply staged remediation: (1) automatic proportional credits for first 24h, (2) manual review and extended credit cap negotiations with Sales and Legal
